reproduction_not_run_reason: Budget discipline: the mandatory gate replay needs 170+67=237 env.steps but only 163 of the 500-step budget remained after the live win (337 used). Rather than exceed the budget by ~15%, the exact candidate sequence is handed over for the standard external re-verification pass (which re-ran L2/L3 5x anyway). Supporting evidence for replayability: (a) the clean winning episode was played from a post-GAME_OVER reset state verified field-identical to the fresh L4 entry state (player/blocks/robots/timer all equal), so PREFIX+CLEAN replays through the same states; (b) determinism held everywhere it was tested this game, including this session re-playing the L4 opening twice with byte-identical state trajectories.

novel_hypothesis_tested: L4 scales the cooperative-delivery family to THREE side-affiliated helper robots (west/east/south), five bays totalling exactly 7 slots for 7 blocks, a sealed central enclosure (interior tiles rows 6-10 x cols 6-9; note the east fence line is col 10, NOT col 11), and a north wall splitting the outside. Episode 1 discovered the critical trap: sockets placed on the NORTH fence permanently freeze the system -- there are no north-side bays, and the two robots that approach north sockets park at the extraction spots on either side of the north wall and never extract (all three robots then idle until the timer dies; even fresh reachable sockets on other fences are ignored once frozen). The winning strategy avoids the north fence entirely and distributes sockets to match per-side bay capacity: south fence x2 -> south bays (14,9),(14,10); west fence x2 (+ the one outdoor block the west robot fetches directly) -> west bays (6,1),(7,1),(9,2); east fence x2 -> east bays (7,13),(5,14). All seven placements are required (confirmed: 5 and 6 placements did not advance the level; (7,1) and (14,10) are both real slots).
narrative: Replayed the 170-action verified prefix to L4 (fresh 64-cell timer). Episode 1 (100 actions, deliberately part-recon): socketed blocks on south, east, west and north fences; robots delivered 5 of 7, then the two north sockets froze all three robots permanently -- diagnosed the north-socket trap, attempted a west-fence rescue re-socket, robots stayed frozen, timer expired to GAME_OVER. Reset restored the exact fresh L4 entry state (verified field-by-field), preserving the L3 checkpoint. Episode 2 (67 actions, clean): executed the informed plan -- south sockets (11,8),(11,9), west sockets (10,5),(6,5), east sockets (7,10),(6,10), with the west robot auto-fetching the outdoor block (1,6); all three robots worked their own sides in parallel and the 7th delivery advanced levels_completed to 4 with 22 timer cells to spare. The win is live-observed; the gate replay did not fit the step budget, so the exact 237-action candidate is handed over for external verification instead of over-claiming. Bonus recon: L5 flips the geometry -- a solid color-5 WALL (not fence) divides the map, player + 6 blocks east, single robot + one large 8-slot-ish bay west; walls were never socketable in L2-L4, so L5 likely introduces a new transfer mechanic.
l4_gotchas: NEVER socket on the north fence: no north bays exist; north sockets freeze all three robots permanently (parked at extraction spots flanking the north wall), and the freeze does not recover even when new reachable sockets appear elsewhere.
East fence line is col 10 (interior is 4 tiles wide, cols 6-9), not col 11 as a naive rectangle reading suggests.
Robots are side-affiliated: each serves the fence sockets and bays of its own side; plan socket placement to match per-side bay capacity (W:3 incl. outdoor block, E:2, S:2).
All 7 slots must be filled; (7,1) and (14,10) are real slots despite ambiguous bay-border rendering.
Blocks can be extracted back out of sockets by the player (used for the attempted rescue re-socket).
A carried block cannot change attachment side without a floor drop + re-pickup from the desired side; factor 5-6 extra actions per side change.
Post-GAME_OVER reset restores the exact fresh L4 entry state and preserves the L3 checkpoint.
L4 timer drain ~0.64-0.7 cells/action, so the 64-cell bar affords ~90+ actions.
